results.title: EC tells Supreme Court Centre’s citizenship scrutiny powers are limited - The Hindu
results.label: yes
results.reason: constitutional_authority/national: EC clarifies its limited power over citizenship for electoral rolls.

notes.subject: polity
notes.why_in_news: The EC clarified the scope of its power to scrutinize citizenship for electoral roll purposes, asserting its authority under constitutional provisions.
notes.fact_box: The EC referred to Section 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, which grants the Centre authority to determine the acquisition of foreign citizenship. The EC's power to scrutinize citizenship for electoral rolls stems from Article 324 and Article 326.

prelims_pointers.text: Article 326: Stipulates that Indian citizenship is a constitutional precondition for entry into the voter list.
Election Commission of India (EC) derives its power to supervise elections from Article 324.
Section 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, deals with the termination of citizenship upon voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship.
The EC submitted its arguments in an 184-page affidavit.

notes.mains_question: Discuss the constitutional limitations and scope of the Election Commission's power to scrutinize citizenship for electoral roll maintenance.
mains_dimensions: Balance between electoral integrity and individual rights
